key_insight: A low-storage dual-time implicit finite-volume solver can efficiently simulate stiff RF capacitively coupled plasma dynamics by decoupling physical time stepping from stability limits and solving the nonlinear system in pseudo-time.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more memory-efficient predictive simulation of multi-dimensional plasma reactors for semiconductor process design and control.
method: Pseudo-time iterations with localized block-implicit relaxation for stiff transport and chemistry
Semi-implicit Poisson coupling to speed electrostatic updates
evidence_signal: The method is validated on a 1D argon discharge benchmark and then extended to 2D cases, showing accurate periodic states and physically consistent potential/heating distortions.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful tuning of the physical time step, pseudo-CFL number, and inner iterations, and the approach still needs verification across broader plasma conditions.
paper_title: A Low-Storage Implicit Dual-Time Finite-Volume Framework for Radio-Frequency Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fluid Simulations
